say: THE MASTER SSOT (owner, 16 Nov, the four step 1): every kind described once. Each kind gives its source, its sheet tab and columns, Find's facets for it in order (`find`), its card (`card`: which field fills the picture slot, which are its tags, which blocks make the body, its tiles), its computed fields (`live`), who may see it and which fields are kept from whom (`see`), and its forms (`forms`, drawn by formOf_). Read by js/kinds.js (written from this file by tools/kinds.js) and nothing else: cardOfItem_, item_, formOf_ and may_ all read KINDS.
hooks: A card or live entry is a column name, or "fn(arg, ...)" naming a global function: args are row (the item's row), live (its computed fields), item, raw, entry (the Find entry), entryRow, pic (its picture), or a JSON literal. A missing function gives the slot's empty value (`lookElse` for look).
formsSay: FORMS FROM THE ITEM SHAPE (foundation 2): a form is an item kind (this file) plus this field list: which fields, their order, type (a FORM kind), caption or placeholder, and `may` (a may_() word) for who sees it; money fields also need may_('prices'), so a child never sees a price. `draft`: "form" keeps each box a draft until saved (the handler drops it on success), "set" is Settings' own (fieldHtml), false none. `fields`: a list, or "groups"/"list" for names the backend sends, typed by `rules`. `{x}` in a name is o.vars.x. Drawn by formOf_ (js/form.js) through renderCard's field/control blocks.

id.say: The item's own id, never reused (MS-0001, EV-0301 ...).

kind.say: Which kind of item it is: one of `kinds` below.

name.say: What it is called; the card's first tag.

tags.say: Its own words (language, era, genre ...), for search, tag cards and topic pages.

body.say: What it says, as renderCard blocks ({ type, ... }); may be empty.

links.say: Ids of other items it points at (a manuscript's writings, an event's figures).

booking.say: Booking, asked in Find one field a step in this order (owner, 13 Nov); each field is a BOOK_STEPS question (book-steps.js) or the hour grid (days, slots). given: the site answers it (bookPrefill_), still a chip. many: several answers, a tap ticks; need: how many before Next. rows: the order the booking card lists them (BOOK_STEPS). A field's `step` is its booking question as data, read by formSteps_ (form.js): q, short (words keys or text); list (fixed options) or from (a source: clients, children, openJobs, subjects, levels, tutors, venues, intervals, seats, hourGrid); when/unless (conditions that empty the list), may (a permission); filter (a row field that must be set, or a named test), label (the row field, or fields in turn, or a named function), sort (a row field), first/last (options put before/after), then (a named step over the whole list); say (an option's shown text: a map, or a named function); check (why an answer is refused), off (why an option is greyed), fallback, lock, set: named functions in BOOK_FNS (book-steps.js). Any name is looked up there first, else read as a row field.

fields.ask: What time? Each tag is one hour.

card-edit.say: the tutor card's edit form (cardEditForm_): its sections' names, typed by rules; a price only for may_('prices').

card-seat.say: the extra seat in pounds, kept as the share in the hidden twin (type `shown`: `show` draws the stored value, `store` turns what is typed back); @family.'s share only for an admin.

card-where.say: Where you teach: an area a tick, rewriting the hidden venues_ok, saved by the card's Save.

extra_seat_rate.label: extra seat: share of your rate, 0–1 (0.5 = half)

extra_seat_cut.label: @family.'s share of an extra seat, 0–2 (blank = the usual)
extra_seat_cut.labelLocked: @family.'s share of an extra seat — set by @family. (blank = the usual)

joined.say: THE PAPER'S CARD, NOT COPIED (owner, 17 Nov): these fields are stored once, on the paper's own row (kind document, same paper_id), and joined onto each of its questions as the file is read (js/library.js libJoinPaper_, the backend's copy in cards-gen.gs). A question keeps one only where it differs (an override); null is none though the paper has one.

sign-join.say: Make an account, asked in Find one field a step (owner, 16 Nov: one form): who it is for, whose email, the names, the email and a 4-digit PIN; sent as the existing `register`. The PIN is held in memory for the call only, never stored. only: asked when an earlier answer is this.

fields.label: Who is the account for?
fields.note: Both are free; teaching starts with "Apply to teach" once you are in.

sign-in.say: Signing in, Find's first step (owner, 13 Nov): the name typed on the blank tag, then the PIN a digit a tag; sent as `verifyLogin` on the last digit. The digits are never kept.

pin-change.say: Settings' Signing in card (owner, 16 Nov: one form): your PIN now, the new one, and it again, a digit a tag; sent as the existing `changePin`. The digits are held for the call only, never stored.

facts.say: WHAT THE OWNER STATES ABOUT A PERSON (owner, 16 Nov): one row a fact, {who, what, value, as_of}. `what` is one of `keys`; a value may be a range ("7-8"). Values age by themselves (`ages`): school_year goes up one each 1 September after as_of, age one each year after as_of. Shown on the person's card to staff (tutors) and admins only (`see`), never to a child or another family. Sent as backend payload `personFacts`; kept in the items tab as kind `fact` (17 Nov). A PIN is never a fact.

food-new.say: the "New food" card in Find (form.js storeSend_): one field a step, any left empty, sent as the one action `item` (mode write).

task-new.say: the "New task" card in Find (form.js storeSend_): one field a step, any left empty, sent as the one action `item` (mode write).

drive_area-new.say: the "New Drive area" card in Find (form.js storeSend_): one field a step, any left empty, sent as the one action `item` (mode write).

findSay: FIND (rule 1.80): a kind's `find` gives its What-for group, its What-kind label, the front door(s) it stands under (`under`), the facets in order, and `draw` (a global that draws its Find card, else findCard). `entries` names the Find entry kinds it covers when they are not the kind itself (an answer page, a timeline, a switched-off door), each overriding those fields. An entry kind named by no kind is never listed or drawn; `see.who` (anyone, signedIn, self, family, staff, admin) decides who is listed it. Labels and order of the facets are data/settings/facets.json. A kind with `from: "store"` (the owner's life and business, 17 Nov) is listed straight from the items tab (form.js storeItems_): a `new` card asking its `store` form, then one card a row, its Edit tile asking the same form prefilled and saving under the same id, and `card.tick` ({f, on, off, label}) a one-tap tile that flips that field; `facetCols` names each facet read off a row's own column.

ledger.say: THE ITEMS AND EVENTS TABS (owner, 16 Nov, go extreme): every Ledger tab is one kind, a card kind's `sheet` above or a storage kind in `stored`; `to` is items unless it says events. An item row is {id, kind, data_1..data_6}: data_1 the row as JSON, or a blob's six chunks. An event row is {at, who, kind, what, item, data}. `id` is a column, or columns joined by ':'. `owner` columns say whose an item is (self and family in `see.who`; staff is a tutor). A non-admin gets only a kind's `sheet.show` columns when it has them, never a `never` column, never a `see.hide.prices` column as a child, never a `see.hide.admin` one. Read, written and logged by the one action `item` (backend/items.gs); every other reader asks core.gs `read(tab)`, which routes a moved kind here. A tab with no kind is in `unmapped`.

unmapped._README: the owner's notes on the file itself, not data

ledger.movedSay: THE KINDS KEPT IN THE ITEMS (or events) TAB (owner, 17 Nov): core.gs read/setCell/addRow route a listed kind there; each has a `~moved` marker row holding its columns. Their old tabs are locked and never read. A new kind is listed here and starts with SCHEMA's columns.

kept.say: KEPT ON THEIR OWN TABS, ON PURPOSE (17 Nov): the library is 39,000 rows of chunked JSON read a few rows at a time by row number (library.gs libIndex_/libContent_). In the items tab, every request that reads any moved kind would load all of it; on their own tabs they are already one item a row ({id, checksum, parts, content_1..6}), described here by each kind`s sheet. claude_notes is written directly by sessions (facts moved to the store, 17 Nov).
